final_assessment: Ran the R-crc-1 size check before promotion rather than letting a reviewer find it, which is what the ruling asks for and what R-crc-9 applied preventively looks like. Result: TEN capabilities against a ceiling of THREE — 3.3x over — and the gap is not scope creep but the charter having been written before the mechanism existed. The charter names three. The mechanism as settled touches orbit-emit-composition, orbit-run-summary-emit, orbit-archive-modifications, orbit-review, orbit-review-external, orbit-report-rendering (the forward recommendation has to RENDER, and D4 owns the report), orbit-orientation (D-rc04-16's status reader), plus orbit-engine-gates, orbit-pr-lifecycle and orbit-conventions — because gate_overridden occurs in SIX baseline specs, not the one the charter implies. Recommended split into three stages, each AT the ceiling and ordered by dependency: rc04a the judgement record (the continuation and readiness slots plus the write-gate ordering rule; three capabilities; gate_overridden keeps being written and the two coexist; ships with ONE reader, which satisfies exit (4)); rc04b the forward recommendation (three capabilities; depends on rc04a only loosely, since a readiness record cites pass TOKENS whether or not those passes carry recommendations); rc04c retire gate_overridden (three capabilities plus the four workflow bodies, and it MUST follow rc04a because continuation/proceed has to exist before the record it replaces can go). orbit-orientation's status reader defers, being the second reader where exit (4) is already satisfied by the first. Named the split's cost rather than leaving it to be discovered: gate_overridden and continuation/proceed coexist between rc04a and rc04c, which is two records for one fact — the exact defect this program keeps catching — accepted deliberately and BOUNDED by declaring rc04c up front rather than hoping for it. The alternative is one stage at 3.3x the ceiling, which is what R-crc-1 exists to prevent and what rc02's six-pass proposal cadence cost. This is a SCOPE call under D-rc04-3 as amended, so it is recorded as a RECOMMENDATION: splitting a chartered stage into three is architecture work belonging to /orbit:architect, not to this exploration.
